Pairwise comparison of joinpoint trends

Source: R/compare.R
jp_compare.Rd

Tests whether the joinpoint regression functions of two cohorts are identical (test of coincidence) or parallel (test of parallelism, equal joinpoints and slopes with different intercepts), using the permutation test of Kim et al. (2004). Every pair of levels of the innermost by-variable is compared within each combination of the other by-variables. The test is carried out with K = max(K0, K1, K2) joinpoints, where K1 and K2 are the numbers selected for each cohort and K0 the number selected for the two cohorts fitted together under the null hypothesis. For each pair whose test rejects the null hypothesis (after any p value adjustment) the AAPCs of the two cohorts of a log-linear fit are compared by a z test with parametric variances, also when the fit used empirical quantile intervals; these follow-up p values are not adjusted.

Usage

jp_compare(
  object,
  type = c("parallel", "coincidence"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_perm = 4499,
  seed = 7160,
  p_adjust = "none"
)

Arguments

object

A joinpoint object with at least one by-variable, fitted with uncorrelated errors.

type

"parallel" or "coincidence".

alpha

Significance level of the test.

n_perm

Number of permuted data sets.

seed

Random number seed.

p_adjust

Method of stats::p.adjust() applied to the p values of the tests of all pairs, for example "holm" when many pairs are compared; the unadjusted p values are kept in p_unadjusted.

Value

An object of class jp_comparison: a data frame with one row per pair and the attributes aapc (AAPC comparisons), fits (null model fits) and p_adjust.

References

Kim HJ, Fay MP, Yu B, Barrett MJ, Feuer EJ (2004). Comparability of segmented line regression models. Biometrics 60:1005-1014.

Examples

d <- subset(us_mortality, cause %in% c("Stroke", "Heart Disease"))
fit <- joinpoint(d, year, rate, by = "cause", kmax = 2,
                 ci_method = "parametric")
cmp <- jp_compare(fit, n_perm = 199)
cmp
#> Pairwise comparison: test of parallel
#> 
#>         group1 group2     test joinpoints k_null k_group1 k_group2 statistic
#>  Heart Disease Stroke parallel          2      1        2        2     732.1
#>  df1 df2 p_value alpha       result
#>    5 186   0.005  0.05 Not parallel
#> 
#> AAPC comparisons (group 1 minus group 2):
#>         group1 group2                  range    aapc1  aapc2 difference lower
#>  Heart Disease Stroke Full Range (1900-1998) -0.02318 -1.472      1.449 1.255
#>  upper statistic p_value significant  ci_method
#>  1.643     14.55 5.5e-48        TRUE parametric
